title: Peat persistence index, Central Kalimantan: persistence of fire activity on peat, 1 Aug to 31 Oct
rule: A persistent peat site is a 0.01 degree cell (about 1.1 km) whose centre lies on peat and where, within one season (1 Aug to 31 Oct), VIIRS S-NPP detected fire on three or more days, or fire was detected again after at least one gap. A gap is a run of two or more days in a row with no VIIRS detection in the cell, between two days with a detection. Each gap is one come-back.
decision: Where a Manggala Agni crew should go back and re-check after the hotspots vanish.

definitions.cell: The 0.01 degree grid of the visibility layer: box 110.7 to 115.9 E, -3.6 to 0.9 N. A hotspot belongs to the cell with column floor((lon - 110.7) / 0.01) and row floor((0.9 - lat) / 0.01), computed on whole thousandths of a degree. lon and lat of a site are the cell centre.
definitions.peat: The cell centre lies inside a polygon of the Global Forest Watch Indonesia peat lands layer (the source polygons, not the simplified ones drawn on the map).
definitions.district: The cell centre lies inside the district outline (geoBoundaries gbOpen ADM2). Only the 14 districts of Central Kalimantan are counted.
definitions.days_detected: Number of days (FIRMS acq_date, UTC) in the season with at least one VIIRS hotspot in the cell. Hotspots are the ones in the season file: type 0, confidence nominal or high.
definitions.night_share: Night detections divided by all detections of the cell in the season (0 to 1, 2 decimals).
definitions.gap: A run of two or more days in a row with no VIIRS detection in the cell, between two detection days of the same season. There is no upper limit on its length inside the season. In a site, each gap gives "from" and "to" (first and last day with no detection), "days", "class", and "missing_sensor_file": true when the catalogue had no file of Terra or Aqua (or both) for one of its days.
definitions.under_cloud_with_a_day_without_a_modis_s: Per season: the "under_cloud" gaps with at least one day on which only one MODIS sensor had a file, so that class rests on a single sensor there.
definitions.come_backs: Number of gaps of the cell in the season: the fire activity was detected again after each of them.
definitions.gap_day_look: What Terra and Aqua recorded for the cell on a gap day (MODIS FireMask of the 1 km pixel at the cell centre, daily composite of all passes): fire when either classed it fire (7, 8, 9); else a cloud-free look with no fire when either saw clear land (5); else cloud when either saw cloud (4); else no usable look (not processed, water, unknown, or no file that day).
definitions.under_cloud: No gap day had a cloud-free look: on every gap day the cell was classed cloud. The quiet days of this gap were not observed, so the zero should not have been trusted.
definitions.seen_quiet: At least one gap day had a cloud-free look with no fire, and MODIS classed no gap day as fire. The place was looked at, nothing was detected, and fire activity was detected again later.
definitions.no_data: Neither of the above and no MODIS fire: no gap day had a cloud-free look and at least one gap day had no usable look at all.
definitions.modis_fire: Terra or Aqua classed the cell as fire on at least one gap day, so the gap exists only in the VIIRS record. Counted apart; these gaps are in none of the three classes above.
definitions.peat_cells_with_fire: Peat cells of the district with at least one VIIRS detection in the season.
definitions.persistent_peat_sites: Peat cells of the district that meet the rule in that season.
definitions.top_sites: Persistent peat sites of the most recent season in which the district has any, ranked by days detected, then by come-backs (ties: west to east, then north to south). At most 40 per district; "persistent_peat_sites_in_that_season" gives the number before the cut.

notes.wording: This describes persistence of fire activity on peat as the satellites recorded it. It does not say that fire was present during a gap, under cloud or anywhere else, and it is not a forecast.
notes.smoke: Thick smoke is usually not flagged as cloud in the MODIS fire mask. A gap day under thick smoke can be recorded as a cloud-free look with no fire, so "seen quiet" does not prove the ground was visible, and "under cloud" is a lower bound of the gaps with no clear view.
notes.exploratory: Exploratory description, written after looking at the data. It is not the registered re-appearance test: the rule differs (0.01 degree cells, any gap of two or more days) and 2019, the season that test locks, is left out entirely and was not read.
notes.detection_limit: A cloud-free look with no fire is not proof that nothing burned: small or smouldering peat fires can stay below the detection limit of both sensors.
notes.provisional: The 2026 season comes from near-real-time FIRMS data and is provisional. From 16 to 31 October 2026 the catalogue has no file of one or both MODIS sensors for part or all of the box, so the class of a gap there rests on one sensor or on none. Each season entry counts the "under_cloud" gaps of that kind, and such gaps carry "missing_sensor_file" in a site.
notes.season_edges: Only 1 Aug to 31 Oct is looked at. A detection before 1 Aug or after 31 Oct is not seen, so a site can have more days and more gaps than counted here.

seasons_not_included.2019: Locked by a registered test (Central Kalimantan and Pulang Pisau, 1 Jan to 31 Oct 2019). Not read, not computed, not emitted.
seasons_not_included.2025: No season file was built for Aug to Oct 2025.

totals_note: Sums over the 14 districts. "total" adds the seasons up, so a cell that qualifies in three seasons is counted three times there (site-seasons).

sources.hotspots: NASA FIRMS VIIRS S-NPP 375 m, as filtered in app/public/ka-data/kalteng_<Y>_season.json (standard processing; 2026 near-real-time, provisional)
sources.cloud_states: NASA MODIS MOD14A1 (Terra) and MYD14A1 (Aqua) Collection 6.1 FireMask, the files listed in visibility_kalteng_<Y>.json (each checked against its recorded sha256), read with pipeline/visibility/build_visibility.py

peat.name: Global Forest Watch, Indonesia peat lands (original: Kementan/BBSDLP peat map), https://gis-gfw.wri.org/arcgis/rest/services/country_data/asia/MapServer/10
peat.license: UNVERIFIED (GFW open data portal; CC BY 4.0 assumed; original: Kementan/BBSDLP peat map)

districts.name: geoBoundaries gbOpen IDN ADM2 (simplified), from BPS, WFP and OCHA ROAP
districts.ids: aoi_id, name and province as in app/public/ss-data/districts/index.json
